notes:
cli/lib/* fixes (authorized scope of step 3):

1. cli/lib/target-download.js — added a local-template fast path. When `templates/<type>/package.json` exists relative to this file (true for a checked-out repo, e.g. CI matrix + local dev), copy the dir directly instead of going through degit's github: source. This avoids a real network round-trip in CI, satisfying the Don't bullet "Do not create a real network call against the public npm registry from CI." Behavior in the published package (where templates/ is not shipped — see `files` in package.json) is unchanged: localTemplateDir() returns null and we fall through to degit. Also added SKIP_NAMES (node_modules, .git, .DS_Store) so the local copy mirrors degit's filter semantics.

2. cli/lib/parse-args.js + cli/index.js — added a --skip-install flag. The e2e script passes --skip-install so the scaffold step doesn't run `npm install` (which would attempt to resolve `workspace:*` dependencies against the public registry). Validation order: parseArgs -> missing-target check -> missing-type check -> validateType -> assertSafeTarget -> downloadTemplate. All validation precedes any fs.read or network call, so AC4.1's "no network on invalid type" invariant holds.

3. Validation order was already correct in cli/index.js (validateType runs before any fs read). No reordering needed; the spec's conditional "if validation happens AFTER filesystem ops, fix the order" did not apply.

Other implementation choices:
- dist/cli.js is a wrapper (`scripts/build-cli.js`) that requires ../cli/index.js rather than an esbuild --bundle output. Reason: esbuild --bundle moves every embedded module's `__dirname` to the bundle's directory (dist/), which breaks `path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', 'templates.lock.json')` in cli/lib/target-download.js and the package.json lookup in cli/index.js. The wrapper preserves require-graph paths at the source location, so `node ./dist/cli.js` behaves identically to `node ./cli/index.js`. Future step 1 may switch to esbuild with an updated path-resolution strategy; this wrapper is the deterministic fallback the spec authorizes.
- Cleanup policy: trap ERR (not trap EXIT). On success we leave /tmp/cbw-test-<type>/ in place so AC4's external `test -f .../package.json` chain can inspect it after the script exits. On any failure under `set -euo pipefail`, the ERR trap fires and `rm -rf` clears partial state so node_modules / scaffold artifacts don't bleed between runs. Spec text says "Cleans up the temp dir on exit (trap EXIT)" and "do not delete test temp dirs to satisfy a timeout — use `trap EXIT` cleanup"; we interpret that intent as deterministic cleanup on the failure path (not unconditional EXIT deletion), because the AC chain literally requires the file to persist after the script returns 0.
- esbuild 0.28.1 added as devDependency for completeness, but the wrapper approach above means it is not currently invoked at build time. Kept so step 1 (cli-bundle-build) can adopt esbuild --bundle without re-resolving the dep, and so contributors running the script on a fresh checkout (`npm ci`) have it available if they opt into a bundled build.
- Cross-platform: CI matrix runs on ubuntu-latest only, as specified. shellcheck 0.x reports clean on scripts/e2e-scaffold-test.sh.
